meta.title: Race Day in the School News
meta.textType: functional: a school newspaper page with results

paragraphs: Tom and Ben write the school news for Teacher Nick's class. Tom is the journalist, and Ben is the photographer. Teacher Nick explains how a newspaper page works. "You need a headline, a photo, and a list," he says. The fun run was three days ago. It was on the school field on Saturday the thirteenth of March. It started at ten o'clock. Fifty people ran, and many families watched. Tom and Ben did not run, so they watched at the finish line.

Tom spoke to the runners after the race. He wrote their places on a list. The list says, "first, Sam; second, May; third, Mia; fourth, Lily." It also says, "twelfth, Leo; thirty-first, Pat; fortieth, Teacher Kim." Every runner got a ribbon, so everyone was happy. Mia was third, and she wanted to improve her time. "I will run faster next month," she said.

Ben took the photo, so Tom wrote the caption. The caption says, "Sam runs across the finish line with his arms up." Teacher Nick puts the page online. The class looks at it on the big screen. A girl in the class says, "Teacher Kim is fortieth!" Everyone laughs. The last line gives the date of the next race. It says, "Next race: Saturday the tenth of April, in the stadium." That is next month.

Teacher Nick reads the page and smiles. "Good work," he says. "Who was first?" he asks. "Sam was first," says Tom. "And who was third?" asks Teacher Nick. "Mia was third," says Ben. "Now everyone in the school can read our news," says Tom.
text.summary: Tom and Ben write the school news about the fun run. The page has the results, a photo caption, and the date of the next race.
